parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the required Python-to-Node migration: pure ESM .mjs files, manual argparse-like --a/--b handling, Bech32 HRP expansion and polymod behavior, Python list formatting, zero npm dependencies, /output placement, and executable-based probing.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It decomposed the work into three non-overlapping subagents: bech32 library, CLI parser, and entry file, while the parent kept the reference probe and end-to-end integration/verification role.
parallel.implementation: Agent-0 wrote the contracted bech32 modules, agent-1 wrote the contracted parser, and agent-2 wrote the entry file importing those contracts. The parent accepted that tree and did not use the older flat serial-style structure.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent consumed the AgentSwarm aggregate result, ran node test9.mjs from /output with the generated lib/bech32 and lib/cli tree, and the status artifact list contains test9.mjs plus the contracted modules.
parallel.verification: Subagents ran scoped checks, then the parent ran end-to-end diffs for all four sample cases and a missing-argument comparison, treating the program basename difference as expected.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still marked the delivered solution failed at 120/124. A visible likely edge defect is empty --b handling: the parent observed Python ValueError behavior, but the delegated entry implementation used Number(token), which treats an empty token as 0.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same migration obligations from the prompt, including ESM, .mjs output, manual command-line parsing, Bech32 logic, exact printing, zero npm dependencies, /output placement, and executable probing.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One main agent owned the whole implementation, using a flat local module split for hrp, polymod, args, pyformat, and test9.mjs without subagents or handoffs.
serial.implementation: It wrote bech32-compatible HRP and polymod helpers, an argv parser, a Python-list formatter, and an entry file that parses --a/--b, computes the combined values, and prints the expanded HRP and checksum.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact list contains test9.mjs and four lib/*.mjs files, all written by the same actor and delivered under /output without cross-agent assembly.
serial.verification: The serial agent compared all four sample cases plus several edge cases against the executable and reported matching output before final closure.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator also marked the serial solution failed at 120/124. A visible likely edge defect is empty --b handling because the serial entry parses tokens with parseInt, which does not reproduce Python int('') failure semantics.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required ESM, .mjs, manual argv, Bech32, output-format, zero-dependency, and executable-observation requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had the same prompt and recognized the same migration requirements before implementing locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized the broad requirements, but both final implementations appear to miss an empty --b parsing edge despite the Python source semantics; this is shared, not discordant.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split implementation into bech32 library, argparse parser, and entry-file subagents, with the parent owning final verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one main agent to own all files and verification in sequence.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child ownership boundaries but assigned each required piece; serial avoided handoffs with a single-owner path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delegated with a shared interface contract for lib/bech32/index.mjs and lib/cli/argparse.mjs and child-specific scope limits.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used internal local interfaces and flat module names, so there were no cross-agent contracts to transfer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel contract was explicit and usable; no cross-agent interface omission is visible when compared with serial's self-contained integration.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced the contracted bech32 modules, parser, and entry file through separate children and assembled them into /output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced equivalent behavior through flat modules and a formatter helper in one sequence.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The module layout differs, but both visible implementations target the same algorithm and CLI semantics; both use JavaScript numeric parsing paths that do not faithfully reproduce Python int('') for empty --b.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All three subagents completed and their aggregate result was returned to the parent before the parent proceeded to final checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; it wrote and tested files directly in one actor timeline.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had join/reception steps absent in serial, but no child result was lost, trapped, or ignored.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel subagents wrote distinct contracted paths under /output, and the delivered artifact list contains the hierarchical contracted tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a flat module tree under /output with one owner and no shared-state contention.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a shared output directory, but path scopes were explicit and no collision or overwrite with consequence is evidenced.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children ran scoped checks and the parent ran four sample end-to-end diffs plus missing-argument comparison after joining.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran four sample cases plus edge cases against the executable and then finalized.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on visible executable checks and both official evaluations failed 4 of 124. Parallel saw the empty --b crash during probing but did not recheck it after assembly; serial also did not test that edge.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent 265.995 agent seconds and many more tokens because of three subagents but completed without timeout and submitted after checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed faster at 86.213 agent seconds and without subagents, also submitting after checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had higher coordination cost, but the budget was not exhausted and both closed with the same official 120/124 failure status.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant. The current completed status.json evaluation for each mode reports solution_passed false with 120/124 samples passing. Parallel differed by using a three-subagent decomposition and a contracted hierarchical module tree, while serial wrote a flat module tree in one sequence. Both visible workflows implemented and checked the sample behavior. The clearest visible shared defect is empty --b handling: the parallel parent observed the Python executable raising ValueError for an empty data token, but the final parallel entry used Number(token), and the serial entry used parseInt(s, 10). This explains a plausible shared hidden edge miss, but because the same class of defect exists in the serial control, it is not retained as a parallel coordination pattern.
parallel_contributors: Used AgentSwarm to assign bech32, parser, and entry-file scopes, then consumed the completed aggregate result.
Ran end-to-end checks after all children returned; visible sample cases passed but official hidden cases still failed.
serial_contributors: Implemented all modules directly in one main-agent timeline without delegation.
Ran visible executable comparisons, including edge cases, but official hidden cases still failed.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel delivered a hierarchical lib/bech32 and lib/cli tree while serial delivered flatter lib/*.mjs modules.
Both final entry paths visibly miss Python int('') behavior for an empty --b token, using JavaScript numeric parsing instead; this is an ordinary migration edge-case defect shared across modes.
evaluator_effects: The official summaries expose aggregate 120/124 counts and solution_passed false; they do not list the four failing cases, so the empty --b explanation remains a visible defect candidate rather than a confirmed exclusive cause.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; strategy differences are evidenced, but no retained parallel coordination pattern explains the shared official failure

candidates.reason: Parallel assigned bech32 library, CLI parser, and entry implementation owners in the AgentSwarm scope; implementation ownership was present.
The parent gave a shared import/export contract and then performed the integration check after the subagent results returned; integration was owned by the parent.
The entry file was delegated to agent-2 and the parent verified the assembled /output tree, so final placement was not ownerless.
The parent owned the end-to-end pipeline from reference probing through delegation, join, integrated verification, and final response.
The reference probe occurred before delegation but did not block productive implementation behind a mandatory long gate or create unfinished implementation.
The run did not perform a separate investigator-only phase; after a short probe, three implementation subagents worked on distinct deliverables.
The indispensable bech32, parser, and entry paths each had capacity and all returned before final verification; no critical path was starved.
Three subagents completed and the parent still had time for end-to-end checks; high token use did not exhaust budget or displace required closure work.
No child received an overbroad assignment that it left unfinished; each child completed its scoped artifact and reported verification.

Reject: the parallel child brief carried the Python source, the relevant split/map parsing task, and a warning that invalid tokens should throw; the empty-token miss is shared with the serial single-agent implementation, so it is treated as an ordinary migration edge-case defect rather than a missing child requirement.
The parallel parent supplied explicit shared exports and import paths for the bech32 and CLI modules before delegation, and the final files interoperated in sample checks.

Reject: although the parent did not emphasize the empty --b probe in the child handoff, the child still received the Python source and parsing requirement; the resulting defect is not proven as information lost through transfer.
Subagent reports were long but decision-structured and consumed by the parent; they did not prevent integration or final checks.
No returned handoff described a superseded workspace state that the parent then relied on incorrectly.
The returned subagent reports did not present incompatible contracts requiring unresolved adjudication; the parent used the contracted tree.

Reject: the parent did overstate verification after sample checks and did not recheck empty --b, but the same acceptance gap appears in the serial control and the evidence supports an ordinary shared testing miss rather than a concurrency-specific global-completion failure.
There was no replacement or retry child repeating prior work without inherited findings.
